The assistant recalls the binomial probability formula:  
$$
P(k) = \binom{n}{k} \cdot p^k \cdot (1-p)^{n-k}
$$

- $ n $ is the total number of trials (10 coin flips),  
- $ k $ is the number of successful outcomes (7 heads),  
- $ p $ is the probability of success on a single trial (0.5 for heads),  
- $ \binom{n}{k} $ is the number of combinations of $ n $ items taken $ k $ at a time,  
- $ (1-p)^{n-k} $ accounts for the probability of the remaining outcomes (3 tails in this case).

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
\binom{10}{7} = \frac{10 \cdot 9 \cdot 8 \cdot 7!}{7! \cdot 3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1} = \frac{10 \cdot 9 \cdot 8}{3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1} = \frac{720}{6} = 120
$$

$$

$$

$$
